prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type glues through cereblon

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the clearest case on the shortlist of a molecular design principle that changed what researchers and clinicians can do. A bifunctional or glue-like molecule gives precise control over recognition and assembly of a ternary complex, and it converts drug action from occupancy-based inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal of the target. Six of eight members place it in their top three, which reflects a real convergence on the chemistry and not only popularity. The concept (Crews and Deshaies, 2001) has been reproduced by many independent groups across many target classes, and clinical degraders are advanced. Including Handa ties the PROTAC strand to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide, which explains the molecular glues and underlies most CRBN-recruiting degraders in the clinic, so the citation covers both strands under one coherent principle.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution and timing. The three-person limit forces a contestable choice among Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex cooperativity), Handa and Ito (cereblon), Sakamoto, Kim and Gray, and the PROTAC and molecular-glue histories are distinct enough that a single citation may look like a compromise. Clinical proof is also still prospective, since no degrader is yet a broadly established approved therapy, so recognition now partly bets on outcomes that have not arrived.

responses.point: Linke ranks degraders first but names Ciulli as the third laureate, citing the structural and mechanistic basis for VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity, and he notes that the molecular-glue branch complicates a clean three-person split.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli case seriously, and the cooperativity work is arguably the most chemically rigorous part of the field. But the drug-like VHL ligands made PROTACs usable, whereas cereblon explains how an already approved drug class works and defines the glue strand that the PROTAC-only citation leaves out. Because most clinical degraders recruit CRBN, I would give the third seat to Handa. I would not call this settled. If the committee wants a PROTAC-centred citation, Ciulli is the right third name, and I could accept that.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation first as a general thermodynamic description of cell organisation in terms of multivalency and phase behaviour, and sees it as squarely physical chemistry.
responses.response: I share her enthusiasm for the physical-chemistry framing, and I ranked condensates seventh mainly on maturity. I disagree that the field is ready now. As Sparr herself notes, and as Aqvist and Linke also stress, physiological relevance in vivo and what counts as true phase separation are still contested, and Pappu and Mittag complicate a clean three-name split. Degraders have a settled mechanism and a clinical pipeline. I would revisit condensates in a few years, and I do not think rank-one support from a single member outweighs that gap.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks base editing third with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli together, and treats genetic code expansion as his second choice, partly on the strength of its conceptual cleanness.
responses.response: I agree on the quality of base editing but differ on attribution. Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees in Liu's laboratory, and the usual Nobel practice is to credit the person who conceived and directed the work, so a Liu-only citation is cleaner and the parallel Nishida and Kondo work is a separate claim. I also worry that the 2020 CRISPR prize makes it look incremental to the wider community. On genetic code expansion, I find it mature and widely used, but I would credit Schultz and Chin and treat Wang as a weaker third.

responses.point: Chabes ranks degraders first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and notes that the credit split among PROTAC inventors, cereblon discoverers and ligase-ligand developers is unresolved.
responses.response: I agree on the configuration and on the open question. Where I would go further is that the question may decide whether the citation reads as one discovery or as two, so the wording of the citation matters: I have framed it as the recruitment of E3 ligases to remove proteins, with cereblon as the mechanistic bridge. I would not accept splitting the prize into separate PROTAC and glue parts unless the committee cannot agree on a unified citation, because a split would cost a seat.

responses.point: Zou ranks molecular-sieve catalysts first and perovskite solar absorbers second, and values structure-determines-function designs with strong industrial reach.
responses.response: The industrial reach is undeniable, but I find B059 diffuse. It spans new frameworks, structure-directing agents and catalyst engineering, and no single discovery is sharply defined, and I think that is the hardest obstacle to a short citation. Perovskites share a milder form of this problem, with at least six credible claimants and unresolved stability and lead toxicity. I rate degraders higher because the discovery is sharply defined and the mechanism is clear.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers Ciulli or Handa as the third laureate, and whether a unified citation can cover both PROTACs and molecular glues.
Whether the absence of a broadly approved degrader drug makes recognition premature for some members.
Whether the Liu-only versus Liu with trainees question and the overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize should move base editing above or below the lipid nanoparticle option.
I have not verified the chronology of the earliest PROTAC and cereblon reports or current clinical-trial status.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. None of the credited candidates are my postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) or Linkoping colleagues. My research overlaps scientifically with Emma Sparr's, but this is not a personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate.
